title: Staffing and costs for 2026 curbside waste collection change
subtitle: Lower affordable transit fares from July, and a longer shared e-scooter and e-bike agreement with Neuron.
overview: The Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee recommended funding and staffing to prepare for the new curbside waste collection contract starting in March 2026. The package includes $1.25 million in 2025, $1.49 million in 2026 and $452,000 in 2027, and 18 temporary positions. The committee said there is no tax levy impact, with 2025 costs offset by one-time Blue Box transition revenue and later years drawn from the Waste Management Reserve Fund {{vote:m2}}. Residents will move to cart-based collection and a four-day collection week, so some will see a new collection day.

The committee also recommended lowering Affordable Transit Program fares from July 1, 2025, so discounts are consistent across fare products {{vote:m3}}. It recommended extending the Neuron Mobility shared e-scooter and e-bike licence for the 2026 to 2029 riding seasons, subject to written agreement each year {{vote:m4}}.
These are committee recommendations, and Council must still adopt them. The committee received a workplace count report and a delegation from Neuron Mobility for information.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended amending the 2025 Waste Management budget by $1.25 million, adding $1.49 million in 2026 and $452,000 in 2027 from the reserve fund, and adding 18 temporary positions, with no tax levy impact {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended reducing Affordable Transit Program fares from July 1, 2025: monthly pass to $47, stored value to $1.35, and MobilityPLUS ticket strip to $6.75 {{vote:m3}}.

The committee recommended extending the Neuron Mobility licence for April 1 to October 31 in 2026 through 2029, if all parties agree in writing each year, with the Commissioner of Transportation Services authorized to sign {{vote:m4}}.

debate: One councillor questioned why the 18 temporary positions returned after budget deliberations and why the detailed business case was not provided earlier, and raised concern about spending from reserves. The Commissioner replied that Council asked at budget for a fuller description of the roles, and that the cuts to staffing discussed at budget related to a different program.

Another councillor asked how many staff had managed recycling before the Blue Box transition to producer responsibility. Staff said staff are not assigned to recycling alone and the full effects will not be clear until the transition is complete, so any redeployment is too early to determine.

On outreach, councillors pressed for strong communications, including working with local municipalities and publicizing medical exemption bag tags. Staff said they were working with municipal communications teams and focusing on small community events, libraries and community centres.

A councillor suggested starting households with the smaller cart to encourage waste reduction. Staff said the contract's service level allows either size, the larger cart is about equal to the current three-bag limit, and smaller default carts may need a later service-level discussion.

Councillors asked Neuron about expanding the service area, helmet use and sidewalk parking. The delegate said expansion would likely need more devices, helmet compliance is hard to measure, and the company uses geofenced parking, photo checks, rebalancing and removal of repeat offenders.
